encounters.title: The Butterfly Dream
encounters.scene: A butterfly drifts across a sky painted on the inside of a glass dome. For a moment, your hands seem like wings. The machine asks whether the dreamer or the dream has the final word.
encounters.question: What does the butterfly dream most strongly challenge?
encounters.hint: Focus on how certain we can be about our present identity, not on whether butterflies are secretly human.
encounters.clue: A vivid dream can feel completely ordinary until you wake.

options.text: That waking experience always feels different from dreaming.
That we can be completely certain which perspective is the waking one.
That dreams can raise genuine questions about identity and experience.
That butterflies can speak human languages.

encounters.lore: Zhuangzi's butterfly story unsettles the confidence with which we label one experience waking and another dreaming. It does not prove that nothing is real. It invites us to ask what grounds our certainty about who we are.

encounters.title: The Joy of the Fish
encounters.scene: A school of silver fish gathers beneath a transparent bridge. One fish darts toward the light, and your companion declares that it must be delighted. A voice from below asks how anyone could know that.
encounters.question: Which response best captures the puzzle about other minds?
encounters.hint: Distinguish seeing behavior from directly having another creature's experience.
encounters.clue: You can observe a smile without feeling the other person's joy yourself.

options.text: We cannot directly inhabit another being's experience, but behavior and context can still give us reasons to understand it.
Nobody can ever have any reason to believe another creature feels anything.
Knowing another's feelings may involve interpretation rather than direct access.
Fish must experience happiness exactly as humans do.

encounters.lore: The exchange about the fish explores what it means to know another being's experience. We may lack direct access to another mind without being forced into total ignorance. The puzzle asks how observation, shared life, and interpretation contribute to understanding.

bossPhases.title: Reconstruct
bossPhases.scene: Zhuangzi appears beside a doorway that alternates between a bedroom and a garden. He invites you to present the puzzle without turning it into a slogan.
bossPhases.question: Which statement best reconstructs the butterfly challenge?
bossPhases.hint: The point is uncertainty about perspective, not a proof that all experiences are false.
bossPhases.clue: Dreams can seem convincing while we are having them.

options.text: We cannot assume our current perspective is unquestionably the final one; a dream can make identity seem settled when it is not.
Everything we see must be an illusion created by insects.
Dreaming can expose limits in how confidently we distinguish experiences.

bossPhases.lore: A strong reconstruction keeps the argument modest but unsettling: experience alone may not certify its own status. The story is an invitation to philosophical humility, not a laboratory demonstration that the world is fake.

bossPhases.title: Spotlight
bossPhases.scene: A lantern singles out one adventurer. The others may send a single encouraging whisper while the lantern waits for an answer.
bossPhases.question: If a dream feels real while it lasts, what follows?
bossPhases.hint: Ask what follows logically, rather than what merely sounds dramatic.
bossPhases.clue: Being mistaken once does not establish that you are always mistaken.

options.text: Every belief about the external world is false.
Feeling certain does not, by itself, guarantee that a belief is true.
Some apparently obvious experiences may deserve further examination.

bossPhases.lore: The spotlight tests the difference between doubt and denial. If certainty can be misplaced, we have reason to examine our beliefs; we do not automatically have reason to reject them all.

bossPhases.title: Reply
bossPhases.scene: The doorway becomes a mirror. Zhuangzi asks whether doubt about dreams leaves us unable to live, learn, or care for one another.
bossPhases.question: Which is the strongest reply to the dream challenge?
bossPhases.hint: A good reply can accept uncertainty while resisting an exaggerated conclusion.
bossPhases.clue: People can have good evidence even without infallible certainty.

options.text: Because I am awake now, I could never have been deceived.
We can have reasonable, revisable beliefs about our world without possessing an infallible test for waking.
Our ordinary practices can still guide action even when philosophical doubt remains.

bossPhases.lore: A thoughtful response need not erase the skeptical challenge. It can distinguish absolute certainty from justified belief, and explain how knowledge and action may remain possible under uncertainty.

insight.title: Butterfly Perspective
insight.description: Once per campaign, add +3 to a party roll by questioning an assumption.

victory: Zhuangzi bows, amused rather than defeated. You have taken the puzzle seriously without mistaking it for a proof. The first doorway opens.
failure: The machine's glow fills every corner of the realm. Your party is Fully Plugged In—but this is a lesson, not an ending. You return to the realm's first challenge with Grip restored to 6.
